dialogue.content: （本日はよろしくお願いいたします。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for coming today. I look forward to our session.)

dialogue.content: （よろしくお願いいたします）
dialogue.English: (Thank you. I look forward to it as well.)

dialogue.content: こんばんは、相談員です。本日はご相談に来てくださりありがとうございます。まず初めにご年齢、性別、本日のご相談内容を教えていただけますでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm a counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. First, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 17歳、女、彼氏と別れてつらいです
dialogue.English: I’m 17, female. I broke up with my boyfriend and I’m hurting.

dialogue.content: 彼氏と別れたことでお悩みなのですね。よろしければ話しやすいところからお話お聞かせください。
dialogue.English: So you’re struggling with the breakup with your boyfriend. If you feel comfortable, please feel free to start wherever is easiest for you.

dialogue.content: 浮気された大好きだったのに
dialogue.English: He cheated on me... even though I loved him so much.

dialogue.content: 大好きだった彼氏に浮気されてしまったのですね、、それはとてもおつらいですよね、、
dialogue.English: Your beloved boyfriend cheated on you... That must be incredibly painful for you.

dialogue.content: もう会えないってなんで？
dialogue.English: Why does he say we can't see each other anymore?

dialogue.content: 彼氏から一方的にもう会えないと言われてしまったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Did he tell you unilaterally that you can’t see each other anymore?

dialogue.content: メールもメッセもブロックされてるっぽい全然連絡取れなくなった
dialogue.English: It seems like he’s blocked my email and messages. I can’t get in touch with him at all.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね、、連絡手段をブロックされてしまいショックですよね、、
dialogue.English: I see... Being blocked from all means of contact must be such a shock.

dialogue.content: いつもの待ち合わせ場所で言われた久しぶりのデートだったのに
dialogue.English: He told me at our usual meeting spot. It was supposed to be our first date in a while, too.

dialogue.content: 久しぶりのデートで会った際にいきなり言われたのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: So he said that to you suddenly when you met for that long-awaited date?

dialogue.content: つらいいっぱいつくしたのに会いたい
dialogue.English: It hurts. I gave him my all, and I still want to see him.

dialogue.content: 行きなり言われたなに言われたのかわかんなくてぼんやりしてたらいつの間にかいなくなってたそのまま
dialogue.English: He said it out of the blue. I couldn’t even process what he was saying, and while I was in a daze, he was gone—just like that.

dialogue.content: そうなのですか、よくわからないままいきなり言われていなくなってブロックされてしまったらショックですよね
dialogue.English: I see. To have him say that out of nowhere, disappear, and then block you before you could even understand—it’s a huge shock.

dialogue.content: とても彼氏さんのことが好きだったのですね
dialogue.English: You really loved your boyfriend, didn't you?

dialogue.content: そう今も好きどうしたらいいかわかんない
dialogue.English: Yes. I still love him. I don't know what to do.

dialogue.content: 失礼しました。今もとても好きなのですね。いきなりそういう状況になってしまったらどうしたらよいかわからなくなってしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: My apologies. You still love him very much. It's completely understandable to not know what to do when you're suddenly put in a situation like this.

dialogue.content: それまでは彼氏にそういったことをしている気配はなかったでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Before this, were there any signs that he might be doing something like that?

dialogue.content: わかんない学校違うから普段はメッセだし
dialogue.English: I don't know. We go to different schools, so we usually just message each other.

dialogue.content: 塾とか行ってればメッセ来ない時間もあるし
dialogue.English: And if he's at cram school or something, there are times when he doesn't message back.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。違う学校というとどうやって出会ったのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Since you go to different schools, how did you two meet?

dialogue.content: 友だちの紹介合コンした
dialogue.English: A friend introduced us—we had a group date.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。年齢は同い年ですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is he the same age as you?

dialogue.content: 先輩ひとつ上
dialogue.English: He's a senior, one year older.

dialogue.content: お付き合いは長かったのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Were you together for a long time?

dialogue.content: 長いよ
dialogue.English: Yeah, a long time.

dialogue.content: 半年続いたもん
dialogue.English: We were together for six months.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね、長く続いてそういった終わり方だと非常に落ち込んでしまいますよね、、
dialogue.English: I see. When a relationship that lasted a while ends that way, it's natural to feel very down.

dialogue.content: 別れるときは何と言われたのでしょうか？もし覚えていればお教えください。
dialogue.English: What did he say when he broke up with you? If you can remember, please tell me.

dialogue.content: 何が悪かったのかなぁ？
dialogue.English: I wonder what I did wrong.

dialogue.content: もうお前とは無理だからって言われた
dialogue.English: He said, “I can’t do this with you anymore.”

dialogue.content: そのような強い言葉を言われたのですね、、それは困惑しますね
dialogue.English: He used such strong words... That must be very confusing.

dialogue.content: なんで？なにが悪かったの？ホテル誘われたとき付いていけばよかった？
dialogue.English: Why? What did I do wrong? Should I have gone with him when he invited me to a hotel?

dialogue.content: なにかが悪かったから別れたのだとお考えなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Do you think you broke up because you did something wrong?

dialogue.content: それがわからないから聞いてるの！
dialogue.English: That's why I'm asking, because I don't know!

dialogue.content: 大変失礼しました。
dialogue.English: My sincere apologies.

dialogue.content: 何か悪いから別れるんでしょう？嫌だから離れるのよね？私のなにが悪いの
dialogue.English: People break up because something's wrong, right? They leave because they don't like you anymore, right? What's wrong with me?

dialogue.content: 一番の理由は彼氏が浮気したからだとおもうのですが、
dialogue.English: I think the biggest reason is that your boyfriend cheated on you, but...

dialogue.content: 嫌だからというより浮気したから離れたのではないのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Rather than him disliking you, isn't it more that he left because he cheated?

dialogue.content: そんなの、浮気しなきゃいいじゃん
dialogue.English: Well then, he just shouldn't have cheated!

dialogue.content: 本当にそのとおりだと思いますね。
dialogue.English: I completely agree with you.

dialogue.content: 恋人と多少不仲になってもやはり多くの人は浮気はしないと思います。そう考えるとやはりあなたは悪くないですよ。
dialogue.English: Even if there's some trouble in a relationship, most people don't cheat. When you think about it that way, you are not the one at fault.

dialogue.content: 私、悪くないの？
dialogue.English: I'm not... the one to blame?

dialogue.content: はい、悪くないと思いますよ
dialogue.English: That's right, I don't think you are.

dialogue.content: いままで色々悩んで辛いなかでよくやってこられましたね。
dialogue.English: You've done so well to get through this, while worrying and hurting so much.

dialogue.content: なんで？
dialogue.English: Why?

dialogue.content: 悪くないのになんで別れなきゃならなかったんだろう
dialogue.English: If I'm not to blame, then why did we have to break up?

dialogue.content: 本当にそのとおりですね、、なんで別れなければならなかったんですかね、、
dialogue.English: That's a very good question... I wonder why you had to break up...

dialogue.content: でも自分が悪くなくても相手のことが原因で別れてしまうこともあるかもしれません
dialogue.English: But sometimes, even if you're not at fault, a breakup can happen because of the other person's issues.

dialogue.content: わからない相手の原因って、浮気のこと？
dialogue.English: I don't understand... By "the other person's issues," do you mean the cheating?

dialogue.content: はい、それも大きな理由としてあるとおもいます
dialogue.English: Yes, I believe that is a major reason.

dialogue.content: なんで浮気したのかなあ？
dialogue.English: I wonder why he cheated.

dialogue.content: 本当にそうですね、なんで浮気したんですかね
dialogue.English: That's true, I wonder why he did.

dialogue.content: ご相談者さまとしては今後どうしていきたいですか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to do moving forward?

dialogue.content: なにが悪かったのか知りたい
dialogue.English: I want to know what I did wrong.

dialogue.content: 別れた理由を知りたいのですね
dialogue.English: You want to know the reason for the breakup, right?

dialogue.content: でも私が悪くなかったと言ってもらえたから、悪くなかったならなんで浮気したのか知りたい
dialogue.English: But since you told me it wasn't my fault, if it wasn't my fault, then I want to know why he cheated.

dialogue.content: そう
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: あと浮気した理由も知りたいのですね
dialogue.English: So you also want to know the reason he cheated.

dialogue.content: そう
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: どうしましょうか？彼氏にはブロックされてしまっていますよね？
dialogue.English: What should we do? He's blocked you, right?

dialogue.content: 別れるなんて受け入れられない、受け入れたくない
dialogue.English: I can't accept that we've broken up. I don't want to accept it.

dialogue.content: 学校まで行く？
dialogue.English: Should I go to his school?

dialogue.content: そうですよね。受け入れたくないですよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. You don't want to accept it.

dialogue.content: そっか、学校はわかっているから直接行くという手もありますね
dialogue.English: I see, since you know which school he goes to, going there directly is an option.

dialogue.content: あとは紹介してくれた友達経由などはどうですか？
dialogue.English: What about going through the friend who introduced you?

dialogue.content: 今までつらすぎて行かれなかった
dialogue.English: It's been too painful, so I haven't been able to go.

dialogue.content: それはそうですよね、、つらすぎますよね、、
dialogue.English: Of course... it's just too painful.

dialogue.content: 友達は、つなぎをつけてくれなくなった向こうが拒否ってるって
dialogue.English: My friend said they can't connect us anymore because he's refusing.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、では直接学校に行くのがいいかもしれないですね、それか塾か
dialogue.English: I see. In that case, maybe going directly to his school is the best idea. Or his cram school.

dialogue.content: 行きたい
dialogue.English: I want to go.

dialogue.content: でも、ストーカーっぽくない？　やばい人にはなりたくない
dialogue.English: But, doesn't that seem like stalking? I don't want to be seen as some crazy person.

dialogue.content: ストーカーっぽいですか？浮気して一方的に別れを告げた彼女が来るのはあたりまえのようにも思えますが
dialogue.English: Do you think it seems like stalking? To me, it seems perfectly natural for a girlfriend who was cheated on and broken up with out of the blue to show up.

dialogue.content: そうかなじゃあ行ってくる
dialogue.English: You think so? Okay, I'll go.

dialogue.content: はい行って直接話をしたらなにか進みそうでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Okay. Do you think talking to him directly will help things move forward?

dialogue.content: わからない会ってくれるかもわからないし、最後の感じだと声掛けたら逃げられるかも
dialogue.English: I don't know. I don't even know if he'll see me, and based on how it ended, he might run away if I call out to him.

dialogue.content: そうされたらどうしますか？
dialogue.English: What will you do if that happens?

dialogue.content: 一回は追いかけると思う
dialogue.English: I think I'll chase after him at least once.

dialogue.content: 一回は追いかけるのですね、それはいいですねそれでも逃げられたらどうします？
dialogue.English: So you'd chase him at least once. That sounds reasonable. What would you do if he still runs away after that?

dialogue.content: その時どう思うかがわかんないまだ追いかけたいのか、もういいやと思うのか
dialogue.English: I don’t know how I’d feel in that moment—whether I’d still want to chase him, or decide I’m done.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか、ではそのあたりは実際にやってみて、ですね。
dialogue.English: I see. So that's something you'll have to figure out when the time comes.

dialogue.content: うん
dialogue.English: Yeah.

dialogue.content: そろそろ終了のお時間となりました。
dialogue.English: It looks like our time is almost up.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: ご相談者さまは彼氏と長く真剣にお付き合いしていてとても誠実な方だなと思いました。途中お話したようにご相談者さまは悪くないと思います。彼氏とお話してみて、前に進めるようになることを願っています。
dialogue.English: I feel that you are a very sincere person who was in a long and serious relationship with your boyfriend. As we discussed, I don't believe you are at fault. I hope that by talking with your boyfriend, you'll be able to move forward.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you.

dialogue.content: それではこちらでカウンセリング終了とさせていただきます。本日はご相談に来ていただきありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: We’ll end the session here. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you.)

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you.)
